model_annotation: The bar chart illustrates the effects of various mBERT and XLM models on different language families and isolated languages, with the x-axis representing language families (IE-Baltic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Romance, IE-Slavic, IE-other, Isolate, Semitic, Uralic) and the y-axis showing the effect size, ranging from 0 to 30. Each language family or group is represented by a cluster of bars, with individual bars corresponding to different models: mBERT-L2 (light blue), XLM-L2 (dark blue), mBERT-R2 (light green), XLM-R2 (dark green), mBERT-B2 (light pink), and XLM-B2 (dark red). Error bars indicate variability in the effect measurements. The chart reveals that the IE-Indic family shows the highest effects for most models, particularly mBERT-R2 and XLM-B2, both reaching approximately 25. In contrast, the Isolate and Uralic categories show very low effects across all models, with values near zero. The IE-Baltic and IE-Germanic families show moderate effects, while the IE-Romance and IE-Slavic families show intermediate values, with the IE-Slavic family showing notably high effects for mBERT-L2 and XLM-L2. The Semitic category shows a mix of moderate and high effects, with XLM-L2 and XLM-B2 showing the highest values, around 20. Overall, the chart demonstrates significant variation in model performance across language families, with some models consistently outperforming others in specific groups.
